title: 曲江二首·其二
titlePy: Qū Jiāng Èr Shǒu · Qí Èr
author: 杜甫
intro: The poem that gave Chinese the phrase “seventy is rare”: a court official pawns his spring clothes to drink by the water, watching butterflies and dragonflies, and begs the spring to stay a little longer.
analysis: 曲江是唐代长安城东南的风景名胜。这时杜甫在朝廷做一个小官，但政治上很不得意。诗一开头就很特别：每天下朝回来，就把春天的衣服拿去当铺换钱，到江边喝得大醉才回家。为什么这样？第二联给了答案：酒债到处都欠着，反正“人生七十古来稀”——人能活到七十岁，自古就少见，不如及时享受。这句后来变成常用语，“古稀”成了七十岁的代称。第三联转写春景，是有名的工整对仗：蝴蝶在花丛深处时隐时现，蜻蜓点一下水面，慢慢地飞。“深深”“款款”两个叠词，把小动物写得又细又美。最后两句对春光说话（拟人）：请你和我一起流转，哪怕只是短暂地互相欣赏，也别违背我。表面是赏春行乐，底下藏着失意和对时光流逝的不安。
analysisEn: Qujiang was a famous scenic lake in the south-east of Chang’an. Du Fu held a minor post at court at the time and felt frustrated and useless. The opening is startling: every day after court he pawns his spring clothes and comes home from the riverside drunk. Why? The second couplet answers: he owes wine debts everywhere, but “since ancient times, few people live to seventy” — so why not enjoy life now? This line became a proverb, and 古稀 (“rare since ancient times”) is still a polite word for the age of seventy. The third couplet turns to the spring scene with a perfectly matched pair of lines: butterflies weave deep among the flowers, appearing and disappearing, while dragonflies dip the water and fly on, unhurried. The doubled words 深深 and 款款 make the tiny creatures delicate and vivid. Finally he speaks to the spring itself, a kind of personification: let us drift along together; even if we can only enjoy each other for a short while, don’t turn away from me. On the surface it is a poem about drinking and enjoying spring; underneath lie disappointment and unease about time slipping away.
background: Du Fu (712–770) wrote this in late spring 758 in Chang’an, where he served as a Reminder (左拾遗), a low-ranking adviser to the emperor. After speaking up for a dismissed minister he had fallen out of favour, and he was sent away from the capital later that year.
pronunciation: 朝回 cháo huí（上朝，不读 zhāo）；尽醉 jìn；酒债 zhài；行处 xíng chù；蛱蝶 jiá dié；深深见 xiàn（同“现”，出现）也有读 jiàn 的；款款 kuǎn kuǎn。
version: 采用通行文本。组诗共两首，这是第二首。

lines.py: cháo huí rì rì diǎn chūn yī
lines.lit: Returning from court, day after day I pawn my spring clothes;
lines.en: Home from court, day after day, I pawn my spring robes

lines.py: měi rì jiāng tóu jìn zuì guī
lines.lit: every day at the riverside I drink until fully drunk, then go home.
lines.en: and walk back from the water drunk each night.

lines.py: jiǔ zhài xún cháng xíng chù yǒu
lines.lit: Wine debts are ordinary — I have them everywhere I go;
lines.en: I owe for wine wherever I go — so what?

lines.py: rén shēng qī shí gǔ lái xī
lines.lit: a human life of seventy years has been rare since ancient times.
lines.en: Few have ever lived to seventy.

lines.py: chuān huā jiá dié shēn shēn xiàn
lines.lit: Butterflies passing through flowers appear deep, deep within;
lines.en: Butterflies thread the flowers, glimpsed deep inside;

lines.py: diǎn shuǐ qīng tíng kuǎn kuǎn fēi
lines.lit: dragonflies touching the water fly slowly, slowly.
lines.en: dragonflies tap the water and drift away.

lines.py: chuán yǔ fēng guāng gòng liú zhuǎn
lines.lit: I send word to the scenery: let us move on together;
lines.en: Spring, I have a message: travel on with me,

lines.py: zàn shí xiāng shǎng mò xiāng wéi
lines.lit: let us enjoy each other for a while — do not turn from me.
lines.en: and for this short while, don’t leave me behind.

words.en: riverside; the edge of the water

words.note: 现代汉语也能说，带点幽默。
现代汉语仍用，如“不同寻常”。
“古稀”今天仍指七十岁，如“年过古稀”。
古代“见”常写作“出现”的“现”。
成语“蜻蜓点水”今天比喻做事浮浅、不深入。
今天多说“款款走来”，形容从容。
现代汉语仍用；也有“风光一时”（得意）的意思。

words.en: to go against; to part from

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 天天醉酒，是借酒浇愁：仕途失意，只好及时行乐。
imagery.en: Drinking every day drowns his frustration — with no future at court, he enjoys what he can.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 花丛里穿梭的蝴蝶，是春天最热闹、也最短暂的样子。
imagery.en: Flowers alive with butterflies — spring at its fullest, and its most fleeting.

imagery.name: 蜻蜓
imagery.zh: 蜻蜓轻轻点水、慢慢飞，写出春天的悠闲和生命的轻盈。
imagery.en: Dragonflies tapping the water and drifting off catch the ease and lightness of spring.
